The paper presents model-agnostic, uniformly valid partial-identification inference based on optimal-transport duality, including randomized-experiment applications.
The paper establishes bootstrap failure outside full differentiability and supplies an alternative resampling scheme for directionally differentiable maps.
The paper develops inference and adaptive inequality selection for intersection bounds expressed as infima or suprema of functions.
The paper studies partially identified fraction-benefiting inference for ordinal or binary outcomes in randomized trials.

Retag primitive L2 learnability as a novel weak law-class condition with a substantive justification, or replace its citation with one supporting existential consistency; separately make clear that E_cf is an estimator-side premise, not a consequence of that condition.

Strengthen the information-hierarchy theorem with a generic strictness characterization or a nontrivial class of CRT laws where roster conditioning strictly improves both endpoints, rather than relying primarily on one enumerated 2x3 witness.
